# parity-fuzz --mode mbident baseline: normalized signatures of KNOWN gaps.
# A divergence whose signature is here is allowed; a NEW one fails CI.
# Regenerate: parity-fuzz --mode mbident --count N --verify 3  (copy NEW-signature lines).
#
# No known gaps — 4000 cases run clean (five seeds).
#
# MULTIBYTE (non-ASCII) parameter NAMES in the BRACED read forms: `${日}`,
# `${#café}`, `${(U)π}`, `${日:u}`, `${(l:6:)Ω}`, `${+ναι}`, `${変数[1,3]}`.
# zsh accepts non-ASCII alphanumerics in identifier names when MULTIBYTE is set
# (default) and POSIXIDENTIFIERS is not — c:Src/utils.c:4347-4350 wcsitype's
# IIDENT arm returns iswalnum(c) for non-ASCII. paramsubst's name-scan sites
# were ASCII-only (`is_ascii_alphanumeric() || '_'`), so every non-ASCII name
# returned "bad substitution". Fixed by routing them through a MULTIBYTE-aware
# predicate that adds ONLY non-ASCII alphanumerics — ASCII parsing is
# byte-identical, so no ASCII form can regress (Bug #1021 in docs/BUGS.md).
#
# Fixed sites (all inside paramsubst, src/ported/subst.rs): the main braced
# name scan (name-start + continuation), the `${#NAME}` length-operator operand
# discrimination, the `${+NAME}` set-test flag, and the simple `$name` /
# `$^name` / `$+name` walks.
#
# ASSIGNMENT (both forms). The mode assigns each scalar via EITHER `typeset
# NAME=val` (builtin path) OR bare `NAME=val`. The bare form exercises the
# lexer's assignment detection (is_valid_assignment_target, c:lex.c:1233
# itype_end(t, INAMESPC, 0)); before the fix the lexer misread `日=x` as a
# command word → "command not found". Read is always braced.
#
# SCOPE — this mode generates ONLY VERIFIED-equal legs (scalar names, assigned
# via `typeset` or bare `NAME=val`, read via a braced expansion). Two legs of
# #1021 are deliberately NOT generated because they are still ASCII-only and
# would fail the gate for a known gap:
#
#   - bare `$日` (no braces) READ — the lexer drops the non-ASCII char after `$`
#     (gettokstr emits a Stringg-only word; `日` never reaches paramsubst), so
#     `$日` prints literally. Only the BRACED read `${日}` works.
#   - `typeset 日=(a b c)` ARRAY creation — the assignment/subscript name scan
#     is a separate leg; zshrs errors "number expected". So the mode assigns
#     scalars only.
#
# NAME SET excludes number-letter codepoints like `Ⅻ` (U+216B ROMAN NUMERAL
# TWELVE): Rust's char::is_alphanumeric() counts them (Unicode Nl) but zsh's
# iswalnum in a UTF-8 locale does not, so `typeset Ⅻ=x` errors "not valid in
# this context" — that case is invalid INPUT (zsh rejects it), not a zshrs bug.
# The is_alphanumeric-vs-iswalnum disagreement only affects these number-letters.
#
# Any divergence here is a regression.
